reviews.title: Maxed settings and great framerates for all games at half the price
reviews.comment: Fits into my SFFPC. I run a 1440p 240hz monitor and I can play any game I want with maxed out settings and frame rates anywhere from 80-240fps depending on title. The 4080 and its super variant will obviously outperform this one, but only by a small margin, and for double the price. I find that this card presents a better value for gamers.  It's the best bang for the buck.
reviews.author: KaTzPJamas

reviews.title: Bought it "Renewed" for a folding rig
reviews.comment:
First things first: I bought this Zotac Gaming RTX 4070 Super card "renewed" and it was indistinguishable from new to my eyes. All accessories, documents, and even the static control bag were all in place. The card SKU itself was correct (eg nobody swapped it for some lower tier card scam) and it has performed exactly as I would expect.
I use this card and another Renewed 4070 Super for a dedicated Folding at Home rig. As such, it's been running nonstop 100% utilization for about four months at this point, sitting in an old X79-era motherboard running Fedora 36 and the Nvidia 535 and now 550 drivers. All it does is crunch proteins and excessively heat my office. All the excessive math means the whole machine is always nice and toasty, with everything in there crunching at its hardest, so of course it makes some noticeable noise. The card isn't quiet, but it's also not intolerable considering it's always at 100%.
For those who care: the 4070 Super is one of the top five cards today for folding speed vs power consumption, also for folding power vs purchase price. Two of these 4070 Supers can crank out the same PPD as a single 4090 at half the cost and about 15% less power. And buying renewed made the price tag even friendlier to my wallet.
Finally, you might also read this same review for an MSI 4070 Super -- it's because I bought them both and have essentially the same feelings (and therefore, review) for each. No, I'm not a bot hehe.
reviews.author: J. Powell

reviews.title: Great for the price!
reviews.comment: I was worried about the size of these new video cards, but this one fit in my case great.  It replaced a rtx quadro 4000 and the fps improvements have been great.  I usually play warzone and my fps went from 60-90 to 120-180.  Although the card is roughly the price of a ps5, I game on pc much more than my ps5 so well worth I to me.  The noise has been quiet and I haven't had any issues with temperature. Overall recommended!
reviews.author: KB Teh

reviews.title: FANTASTIC GPU! LOVE THIS UPGRADE!
reviews.comment: I absolutely love this GPU man...it is a beast...if you are looking for something that is not insanely priced but still want, in my opinion, a top tier performing GPU than this is the one for you...I'm not sure how people call this mid tier...maybe the price is mid tier but the performance is right at that top tier threshold no question about it...it absolutely crushes anything 1440p and with the wizardry known as DLSS upscaling it can easily handle 4k gaming...I upgraded from the 3060 ti, which was also a fantastic GPU, for anyone buying on a budget i highly recommend it...but the performance difference is incredible...i can't say enough good things about this GPU!
reviews.author: Frank G.

reviews.title: Excellent card, runs cool and quiet
reviews.comment:
The smaller size is fantastic for fitting into cases that don't have room for a gigantic GPU  . And despite this smaller size, it does not run hot or make a lot of noise.
I did use the tuning tools to make the fan speeds more aggressive to keep it cool at lower performance points (the fans didn't want to spin up fast until it was getting hot, 65°c or so) and I also turned the power limit to 110% otherwise it kept throttling down the core speed.
Both free and easy fixes to small problems, and the ard performance is fantastic.
reviews.author: Amazon Shopper
